_: Every number the compressor lesson says. MEASURED off renders on 2026-09-04, never assumed. Predictions in predict.py were written BEFORE any of it was rendered.

material.tone: one held A3 sine from the poly synth, 7.5 beats at 100 BPM
material.drums: kick/snare/hat programmed note by note from sine + square. No sample is loaded anywhere.

d1_threshold_and_ratio._: over = 12 dB by construction (threshold derived from the MEASURED dry peak), hard knee, so the prediction is the plain ratio line.

d1b_why_it_is_not_exactly_9._: ⭐ THE BEST BEAT IN THE EPISODE AND IT WAS NOT PLANNED. The static curve is an idealisation; the detector is a PEAK follower that decays between the peaks of the wave, so steady-state reduction falls slightly short. CONFIRMED by three points, not asserted: the shortfall closes monotonically as release lengthens.

d2_attack._: Same drum hit, same everything, only attackMs changes. Attack is not 'how fast it works' — it is HOW MUCH OF THE TRANSIENT YOU KEEP.

d3_release._: RE-SHOT WITH A PAD. In cut 1 the two settings differed by 11.5 dB but at -39.9 vs -51.5 dBFS -- the information lived in the drum TAIL, because between hits NOTHING ELSE WAS SOUNDING, and 25-35 dB below the film's own level is under a laptop speaker's floor. Pumping is heard on something that SITS UNDER the hits, so a held pad was added at a level you can hear.
d3_release.material: kick/snare/hat + a held saw triad (pad gain 0.08), 4 bars at 100 BPM, 1.5 s of tail
d3_release._headroom: The pad MUST clear the threshold by more than the knee half-width. At pad gain 0.12 it cleared by only 1.7 dB, the compressor never let go, and gain reduction sat pinned at 15-18 dB for the whole render with no recovery to show at all.
d3_release._shortfall: Short of the 8.55 prediction because the detector is a PEAK detector with a fixed 5 ms decay, so steady-state reduction lands slightly under the static curve.
d3_release.THE_LINE: Fast lets go COMPLETELY between hits (median 0.00 dB). Slow NEVER lets go at all -- its least-reduced moment in the whole loop is still -2.17 dB.
d3_release._not_matched: DELIBERATELY NOT LOUDNESS-MATCHED. The 2.7 LU difference IS the release still holding the bed down between hits. Matching it away would convert the lesson into 'the kicks stand taller', one step removed from the point. ONE common gain, stated on screen. This does not contradict demo 5: that one compares compressed against uncompressed with makeup; this compares two settings at equal gain.

d4_knee._: The demo nobody does: a tone 2 dB BELOW threshold. A hard knee is not working at all; a soft knee already is.
d4_knee._agreement: The gain computer transcribed into anim_knee.py predicts 1.5625; the render measured 1.52. 0.04 dB apart.
d4_knee._bound: max gap = slope * knee / 8, largest exactly AT the threshold. NO setting and NO signal gets past ~2.85 dB on this plugin. Loudness JND is about 1 dB ideal and worse on a small speaker, so this is at the edge of perception BY CONSTRUCTION.
d4_knee.HONESTY: The chapter must SAY you will not hear it on laptop speakers. That is the lesson -- a soft knee is called gentle because it is gentle -- not a defect in the demo, and it must not be softened into 'listen closely'.

d5_makeup._: Why every compressor A/B you have heard is a lie. Gentle 3:1, soft knee — the setting a mix engineer actually reaches for.
d5_makeup.surprise_peak_note: ⭐ AT EQUAL LOUDNESS the compressed take PEAKS 4.5 dB HIGHER (-6.09 vs -10.59 dBFS): a 10 ms attack passes the transient, then makeup lifts it. Compression did not reduce the peaks — it raised them. This is why a limiter follows a compressor.

d6_mix._: Parallel ('New York') compression: density back without flattening the transient — impossible fully wet.

bit_exact_bypass_at_mix0._: The docs CLAIM mix:0 is a bit-exact bypass. VERIFIED three ways rather than repeated.

d6_mix.ab_is_unlevelled: ⭐ CHANGED 2026-09-05: the A/B is NO LONGER loudness-levelled. The levelled version put the 19.3 LU collapse on a card while only the transient half was audible — a number on screen the ear could not check. One shared static gain (+12.581 dB, chosen from the louder file's peak) is applied to both halves, so the 19.3 LU really plays.

_RECUT_2026-09-05: Demo 3 was RE-SHOT and demos 3 and 4 gained manim charts, because the user reported they could not hear either comparison on MacBook Pro laptop speakers. They were right in both cases and neither was a speaker fault. Cut 1's numbers are kept verbatim in MEASUREMENTS-cut1.json.

intro_diagram._: Chapter 0's picture is MEASURED, not drawn: the 20 ms peak envelope of the SAME two renders demo 3 plays (d3p-dry.wav and d3p-fast.wav), so the opening image of a predict-then-measure film is not the one invented thing in it. introenv.py writes introenv.json; anim_intro.py draws it.

AUDIBILITY_AUDIT_2026_09_05._: USER RULE 2: check that every produced sound can REALLY be heard. Measured on the FIRST 3 s of each A/B pair -- the window the film actually plays -- as integrated LUFS and sample peak, both RAW and after the assembler's loudnorm. A DIFFERENCE IN dB IS NOT A DIFFERENCE YOU CAN HEAR: the absolute level it lives at is the other half of the answer.
AUDIBILITY_AUDIT_2026_09_05.THE_DEFECT_FOUND: assemble.py loudnorm-normalises EACH HALF of an A/B separately unless the stage sets normalize:false. Demos 1, 2 and 4 did NOT set it in cut 1. MEASURED: demo 1's 8.90 LU difference and demo 4's 1.60 LU difference both came out at +0.00 LU -- the two halves were made equally loud by the assembler, so the A/B the narration described could not be heard AT ALL, for a reason no gate in this rig measures. Demo 2's 9.60 LU became 2.20 LU. All three now set normalize:false.

d1_threshold_ratio.verdict: AUDIBLE once normalize:false -- 8.9 LU is enormous and it lives at -16 to -25 LUFS, well inside a laptop speaker's range. Was INAUDIBLE in cut 1.

d2_attack.verdict: AUDIBLE. One common +9.562 dB (chosen from the louder file's peak, ceiling -1.5 dBFS) puts the transient at -1.5 dBFS; the difference is a 12.95 dB peak at the top of the scale, not a tail.

d3_release.pair: release 30 ms vs 800 ms, WITH the pad
d3_release.verdict: AUDIBLE after the re-shoot, and this is the one that was fixed at SOURCE rather than warned about. 2.7 LU at -20 LUFS on a sound that is present throughout, against cut 1's 11.5 dB at -39.9/-51.5 dBFS in a tail.

d4_knee.verdict: NOT RELIABLY AUDIBLE, AND THAT IS THE LESSON. The level is fine (-16 to -18 LUFS); the SIZE is the problem, and it is bounded at 2.25 dB here and 2.85 dB at the widest ratio this plugin allows. The chapter says so plainly and carries the point on the chart.

d5a_makeup_unfair.verdict: AUDIBLE, and 1.9 LU is exactly the size the chapter claims -- it is meant to be a small, unfair-feeling advantage, not a dramatic one. normalize was already false.

d5b_makeup_matched.verdict: AUDIBLE AS A DIFFERENCE IN CHARACTER, NOT IN LEVEL -- by construction. 0.1 LU apart is the point; what moves is the 4.5 dB of peak.

d6_mix.verdict: AUDIBLE, unmissably. The wet half sits at -37.4 LUFS, which is very quiet -- and the chapter says so, because the collapse IS the demonstration.

d1b_detector_shortfall.verdict: INAUDIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION and never claimed otherwise: hundredths and thousandths of a decibel. The chapter now says out loud that these are far too small to hear and that the arithmetic, not the ear, is the evidence.
